import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# For a meaningful visualization, load the full standard titanic dataset.
# Visualizing only the 5 provided rows would not be insightful.
df = sns.load_dataset('titanic')

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", context="talk")

# Create a figure and a set of subplots
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create a bar plot showing survival rate by class, faceted by sex
sns.barplot(
    data=df,
    x='class',
    y='survived',
    hue='sex',
    palette={'male': '#5E88B8', 'female': '#E5A749'},
    ax=ax,
    order=['First', 'Second', 'Third'],
    saturation=0.9
)

# --- Customize the plot for clarity and impact ---

# Set titles and labels
ax.set_title('Titanic Survival Rate: A Tale of Class and Gender', fontsize=20, weight='bold', pad=30)
fig.suptitle('Women in higher classes had a significantly greater chance of survival', fontsize=14, y=0.93, style='italic', color='gray')
ax.set_xlabel('Passenger Class', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel('Survival Rate', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)

# Format the y-axis to show percentages
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.PercentFormatter(xmax=1.0, decimals=0))
ax.set_ylim(0, 1)

# Add data labels on top of each bar
for p in ax.patches:
    ax.annotate(f"{p.get_height():.1%}",
                (p.get_x() + p.get_width() / 2., p.get_height()),
                ha='center', va='center',
                fontsize=12,
                color='black',
                xytext=(0, 12),
                textcoords='offset points')

# Customize the legend
ax.legend(title='Sex', loc='upper right', frameon=True, shadow=True)

# Remove top and right spines for a cleaner look
sns.despine(ax=ax)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.95])

# Save the resulting plot to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')

plt.close()
